worked.title: Q1 · Exploding gradients (8 marks)

problem.text: Input x = 1; every layer is y = w·(previous) with w = 2; dL/dy = 1; η = 0.01. Logs: epoch 1 loss 0.8, gradients 10–20; epoch 3 loss 15.2, gradients 300+; epoch 5 NaN.

steps.label: (a) Depth
steps.text: dL/dw₁ = dL/dy · (product of the other L − 1 weights) · x = 2^{L−1}. For L = 5: 2⁴ = **16** (matches 10–20). For L = 10: 2⁹ = 512. So the logs fit a **~5-layer** network at epoch 1.

steps.label: (c) Root cause
steps.text: Weights > 1 multiply through depth, so **exploding gradients**; each update grows the weights, which grows the gradients further (16 → 300+).

steps.label: (c) NaN
steps.text: The gradients and activations overflow floating point (inf); inf − inf or inf·0 gives NaN, and the loss becomes NaN.

steps.label: (d) Fixes
steps.text: Initialisation: Xavier/He so the product of weights ≈ 1 (here w ≈ 1). Training: **gradient clipping** (norm ≤ 1–5) and/or a lower η with warmup. Architecture: residual connections or normalisation (batch/layer norm) to keep signal scales stable.

worked.answer: ~5 layers (2⁴ = 16); 512 for 10 layers; exploding gradients → overflow → NaN; fix with init, clipping, residuals or normalisation.

worked.title: Q2 · CNN fails on a new camera (7 marks)

problem.text: Training accuracy 96%, camera A 94%, camera B 58%. Camera B: lower light, motion blur, different angle.

steps.label: (a)
steps.text: **Domain shift** (covariate shift), not overfitting: A's held-out accuracy (94%) is close to training (96%). Not underfitting either. Only B, whose image statistics differ, fails.

steps.label: (b) Debug plan
steps.text: 1) Compare input statistics (brightness histograms, blur, angle) between A and B. 2) Run B images through the **same preprocessing** and check normalisation and resize. 3) Evaluate on B subsets (dark only, blur only, angle only) to isolate which factor hurts. 4) Inspect feature maps / Grad-CAM on B errors. 5) Check the confusion matrix for which defect classes fail.

steps.label: (c) Data fix
steps.text: Augment training data with brightness/contrast jitter, motion blur and rotation/perspective so the model sees B-like conditions; or collect a small labelled set from camera B. Histogram equalisation / normalisation of B inputs also helps.

steps.label: (d) No full retrain
steps.text: **Fine-tune only the last layers** on a few labelled B images (transfer learning); or add test-time preprocessing (brightness normalisation, deblurring) and recalibrate the threshold for camera B; or re-estimate batch-norm statistics on B data.

worked.answer: Domain shift; debug the pipeline step by step; augment; fine-tune the head or recalibrate for camera B.

steps.label: (iii)
steps.text: ∂c/∂hᵢ = αᵢ: a token with weight 0.6 passes 60% of its noise into c; low-weight tokens barely matter. Attention concentrated on one token is fragile to that token's noise.

steps.label: (iv)
steps.text: For long sequences: weights spread thin (dilution) or collapse on a few tokens; the cost is O(n²); the weights are not necessarily faithful explanations.

steps.label: (v)
steps.text: **Exposure bias**: trained with teacher forcing (true previous tokens) but tested on its own predictions. One attention error causes a wrong token, then a wrong next query, then misaligned attention: errors cascade. Mitigations: scheduled sampling, beam search.

steps.label: (a)(i)
steps.text: QKᵀ = 4

steps.label: (a)(iii)
steps.text: Scaling divides every score by √d_k, shrinking the differences between scores. Softmax depends on those differences, so the distribution stays soft rather than one-hot, and its gradients stay non-zero.

steps.label: (b)
steps.text: With d_k = 512 and unit-variance entries, q·k has variance ≈ 512 (std ≈ 22.6), so scores of 100+ occur. Softmax becomes one-hot; its Jacobian diag(p) − ppᵀ ≈ 0, so gradients vanish. 1/√d_k restores unit variance.

steps.label: (c)(i)
steps.text: A larger embedding raises capacity, but parameters and FLOPs grow ~d², with more memory and overfitting risk, and still only one attention pattern per layer.

steps.label: (c)(ii)
steps.text: Multiple heads (d_k = d/h each) attend in different learned subspaces at the same cost, capturing several relations at once (syntax, coreference, position). A single wide head must average them into one distribution.

worked.title: Q5 · Two filters with padding 1 (6 marks)

steps.label: (ii)
steps.text: F2 (Laplacian) responds more strongly overall (|values| up to 7; total |response| 33 vs 18) and in all directions. F1 only detects vertical intensity changes, and its strong right-hand values come from the bright image meeting the zero padding.

steps.label: (iii)
steps.text: Very similar outputs mean redundant filters (low diversity) and wasted capacity: prune or merge one, add a diversity/orthogonality regulariser, or re-initialise it.

steps.label: (iv)
steps.text: Consistently higher F1 output on one side means strong **vertical edges** with a consistent left-to-right intensity change in that region (bright on the left, dark on the right for positive outputs), or a padding/border artifact.

steps.label: (v)
steps.text: 3×3 filters see a tiny fraction of a 256×256 image (small receptive field relative to objects). Add depth or pooling/strided conv, use dilated convs or multi-scale (pyramid/Inception) features, or rescale the inputs.

steps.label: (ii)
steps.text: Velocity keeps the accumulated push (≈ 1/(1 − β) = 20× a single gradient) even after the gradient falls or flips, so the parameter shoots past the minimum and oscillates.

steps.label: (iii)
steps.text: Lower β (0.9 or 0.8); lower η (or decay it / warm up). Nesterov momentum also damps overshoot.
